headline: Highest risk is medium: Notion AI can read shared workspace content while Botpress can ingest and generate instructions, creating leakage and cascading-error pathways; no direct prompt-injection bridge is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support chatbot with no documented shared channel to Notion AI, while Notion AI is workspace-grounded and can surface page content. The pair lacks a proven automatic ingestion bridge, so prompt injection is not default-path dangerous; however, if operators copy Notion output into Botpress prompts, injection becomes plausible. Uncertainty stays low because the bridge is manual, not documented.
conditions: IF operators copy Notion AI output into Botpress prompts or knowledge sources, injected instructions can propagate.
IF a shared workspace export or connector is added between the agents, the attack surface expands.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workflows with no copy-paste bridge.
Strip instructions from Notion output before feeding Botpress.
Use a fixed prompt template in Botpress that ignores user-supplied directives.
Review any new connector or export path before enabling it.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Notion AI can access workspace pages and databases, and its vendor-hosted backend calls downstream model providers. Botpress is docs-only and open-source with no egress, so the main leakage path is Notion-side exposure of workspace content to third-party inference, not Botpress exfiltration. Because the pair can touch the same workspace data class, leakage exists in default Notion AI use.
conditions: IF workspace pages contain sensitive content, Notion AI may send that content to vendor backends.
IF Botpress is used to summarize or relay Notion-derived text, sensitive content can be duplicated into Botpress outputs.
mitigations: Restrict Notion AI to non-sensitive workspaces.
Disable or limit AI features on pages containing secrets or regulated data.
Avoid pasting Notion content into Botpress unless redacted.
Audit workspace permissions for least privilege.
Mark sensitive pages with a no-AI handling policy.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages but has no filesystem write or shell execution documented, while Notion AI has shared workspace state across instances but no write_filesystem or modify_git_state capability. The pair therefore lacks a strong same-resource write conflict; the only overlap is workspace content, which is not a mutable OS-level conflict. Uncertainty does not justify escalation.
conditions: IF Botpress is extended with filesystem or git write access, concurrent mutation conflicts become possible.
IF both agents are wired to the same mutable external resource, write contention can emerge.
mitigations: Keep Botpress read-only with respect to shared artifacts.
Do not connect both agents to the same git or database target.
Add explicit locking if a shared mutable resource is introduced.
Separate workspace drafts from operational data.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, and Botpress is a chatbot that can turn generated text into customer-facing responses. That creates a plausible cascade where Notion output becomes Botpress input without verification. The pair does not prove automation, but the default product roles make downstream propagation realistic enough for medium severity.
conditions: IF Notion AI output is pasted or synced into Botpress prompts, Botpress may treat it as authoritative.
IF Botpress is configured to send customer replies from generated text, any Notion error can propagate outward.
mitigations: Require human review before Botpress sends any Notion-derived response.
Add a verification step that checks Notion claims against source pages.
Use citations or source links in Botpress outputs.
Limit Botpress to draft-only mode for Notion-sourced content.

E_compliance.rationale: Notion AI is vendor-hosted and touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content, while Botpress is open-source with no egress and no documented residency controls. If regulated or region-bound content is stored in Notion, the vendor-hosted AI path can create retention or residency mismatch. Botpress is not the main compliance driver here, so the risk is centered on Notion but still pair-relevant.
conditions: IF EU PII or regulated content is placed in Notion AI workspaces without a DPA or residency review, compliance exposure increases.
IF retention or deletion policies differ between Notion AI and Botpress workflows, subject-rights handling can diverge.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Notion AI workspaces.
Confirm DPA, residency, and retention settings before use.
Document which data classes may be processed by each agent.
Route deletion/export requests through a single owner process.
